Context: `ultext(Source Information)`: On `text(May 11, 1846)`, President James K. Polk delivered the following message to Congress. Polk, a southern slave-owner supported the expansion of slavery westward. Polk began his speech by stating that he had tried diplomatic measures to resolve differences with Mexico for the past `text(8 months)`. Congress voted to declare war two days later by a vote of `174` to `14`.
Title: Source D
Content: :box:The Mexican forces at Matamoros assumed a belligerent [hostile] attitude, and on the `12^text(th)` of `text(April)` General Ampudia ... notified General Taylor to break up his camp within `text(twenty-four hours)` and to retire beyond the Nueces River, and in the event of his failure to comply with these demands announced that arms, and arms alone, must decide the question. But no open act of hostility was committed until the `24^text(th)` of `text(April)`. On that `text(day)` General Arista, [Mexican commander] ... communicated to General Taylor that “he considered hostilities commenced [started] and should prosecute [continue with] them.” ...The cup of forbearance [patience] had been exhausted even before the recent information from the frontier of the Del Norte. But now, after reiterated menaces [repeated threats], Mexico has passed the boundary of the United States, has invaded our territory and shed American blood [killed Americans] upon the American soil. She [The United States] has proclaimed that hostilities have commenced, and that the `text(two)` nations are now at war.
